stem: Kavya walks 8 km towards the West. She then turns right and walks 5 km. In which direction is she now moving?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Turning left from West gives South; selecting South confuses left and right turns.
Facing West, a right turn is a 90-degree clockwise rotation: West + right = North.
Reversing the movement direction (treating West as East then turning right gives South; or turning twice) yields East by an orientation reversal error.
Ignoring the right turn entirely and continuing West omits the stated constraint of turning.

explanation: Facing West, a right (clockwise) turn brings the person to face North. Compass clockwise: W + 90 CW = N.

explanation_sections.punchline: A right turn from West points you North, not South.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: identify facing direction (West), apply right turn (clockwise 90 degrees): W -> N. The 8 km walked does not change the facing direction used to interpret the turn.
explanation_sections.lesson: Right = clockwise. From any direction, right turn advances clockwise: N -> E -> S -> W -> N.
explanation_sections.timing: Under 30 seconds. The sole trap is confusing left and right, which gives South.
